$comment: Where every painted face is, measured off the painting itself.
fx / fy  the midpoint between the eyes, as a fraction of the FILE's width and height.
ipd      the eye-to-eye distance as a fraction of the FILE's width; the scale handle.
For a head rolled out of the vertical (Tidus, Wakka, Yuna, Rikku, Lulu) it is the
true separation, the diagonal, not its horizontal projection. For a near-profile
with one eye on camera (Auron, Kimahri, Bahamut, Ixion, Valefor) it is the
human-equivalent value that lands the head at the roster's scale, and fy comes
from that one eye.
px       the file's real pixel size when it was measured. A re-roll that changes the
canvas invalidates the row, and tests/unit/ui-portrait-face-crop.test.ts fails
the build when the file on disk stops matching -- which is exactly how Auron
shipped cropped through the chin last round and nothing noticed.
Measured 2026-09-18 with tools/portraits/measure-face-crops.mjs: each eye read off a
window of the painting under a grid labelled in FILE PIXELS, so the number under the
crosshair is the number the row wants. Regenerate the probes after any art re-roll:
node tools/portraits/measure-face-crops.mjs probe <id>
and re-render the acceptance sheet before believing a row.
tight    true when the painting is a closer close-up than the house framing (eyes wider than
0.34 of the file, or too near its top edge). The tile cannot zoom out past the file, so
the cover clamp pins it; the guard test then proves the pin and allows the eye line
and head scale the painting forces. Never set it to excuse a wrong row.
